comparison: Both evaluate claims C1-C4 regarding SOCE requirement in dopaminergic neurons for flight. OpenEval focuses on genetic manipulations and anatomical specificity. Peer review additionally includes C5-C6 (temporal control) in the same evaluation, affirming the core finding with explicit reviewer quotes describing the study as 'solid' and 'carefully performed.'

OpenEval evaluates C5-C6 (temporal control via TARGET system) separately, emphasizing critical developmental windows. Peer review groups C5-C6 with C1-C4 in a single evaluation, accepting all as part of the core SOCE finding without distinguishing temporal aspects.

Both evaluate transcriptomic findings C8-C11 as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes multiple analytical approaches (three DEG methods, trajectory analysis). Peer review additionally includes C12 (GO analysis identifying Set2) and explicitly quotes reviewers affirming the altered gene expression profile with 'validated' and 'rigorous' methodology.

OpenEval evaluates C12-C18 (Set2 as downstream effector) with emphasis on bidirectional genetic evidence. Peer review evaluates C13-C22, combining Set2 findings with H3K36me3 mechanistic data, and explicitly quotes reviewers describing Set2 and E(z) as central to the 'transcriptional feedback loop.'

Both address C12 (GO analysis identifying Set2). OpenEval groups it with comprehensive Set2 validation (C12-C18). Peer review groups C12 with transcriptomic findings (C8-C12), treating it as part of the RNA-seq analysis rather than Set2 validation.

OpenEval evaluates C19-C22 (H3K36me3 mechanistic evidence) separately from Set2 validation. Peer review combines C19-C22 with Set2 findings (C13-C18) in a single evaluation, treating histone methylation as integral to the Set2 mechanism rather than a separate line of evidence.

Perfect alignment on C23-C26 (E(z) upregulation and H3K36me3/H3K27me3 balance). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes pharmacological rescue by GSK343 as functional validation. Peer review explicitly mentions 'histone modifiers, Set2 and E(z)' as part of the accepted mechanism.

Perfect alignment on C27-C32 (Set2 functional effects on Ca2+ signaling). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes bidirectional changes in gene expression. Peer review explicitly quotes acceptance of regulation of 'muscarinic acetylcholine receptor and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor.'

High overlap on Trl identification and validation (C33-C39 in OpenEval; C33-C41 in peer review). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of computational, genetic, and molecular validation. Peer review additionally includes C40-C41 (Trl knockdown effects) and explicitly quotes the 'Orai-Trl-Set2 pathway.'

OpenEval evaluates C40-C41 (Trl knockdown/overexpression) as part of UNCERTAIN evaluation (R9) due to weak CamKII rescue and lack of direct biochemical evidence for Trl activation. Peer review groups C40-C41 with Trl identification (C33-C39) as SUPPORTED, accepting the proposed mechanism without questioning CamKII evidence.

Both address C42-C43 (Trl transcript levels unchanged, overexpression cannot rescue). OpenEval groups these with C40-C41 and C92 in UNCERTAIN evaluation questioning CamKII mechanism. Peer review evaluates C42-C43 separately as SUPPORTED, accepting them as evidence that SOCE acts upstream of Trl activation.

Both address C92 (CamKII-mediated Trl activation). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to weak rescue and lack of direct biochemical evidence. Peer review groups C92 with C76-C81 (background on CamKII and Trl) as SUPPORTED, accepting the proposed mechanism as part of the validated pathway.

Perfect alignment on C44-C47 (ion channel downregulation and loss of KCl responses). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistent demonstration across multiple assays. Peer review explicitly quotes acceptance of 'voltage gated calcium channels' regulation as part of the Orai-Trl-Set2 pathway.

Perfect alignment on C48-C56 (VGCC regulation and requirement). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive evidence showing ensemble of channels required. Peer review explicitly states pathway 'modulates the expression of voltage gated calcium channels, which, in turn, are involved in dopamine release.'

Perfect alignment on C57-C63 (activity-dependent maturation model). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes bidirectional perturbations and multiple rescue approaches. Peer review accepts findings as demonstrating importance of proper excitability with 'validated methodology.'

Both address C64 (GSK343 rescue correlation). OpenEval groups C64 with structural changes (C65-C67) emphasizing super-resolution microscopy findings. Peer review evaluates C64 alone as pharmacological validation of PRC2/H3K27me3 mechanism, accepting without question.

High overlap on structural and functional consequences (C65-C67 in OpenEval; C65-C69 in peer review). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes structural changes in axonal arborization. Peer review additionally includes dopamine release findings (C68-C69) in same evaluation.

Both address C68-C69 (dopamine release via GRAB-DA sensor). OpenEval evaluates separately, noting partial rescue suggests additional mechanisms. Peer review groups with structural findings (C65-C67), explicitly stating pathway is 'involved in dopamine release' as accepted functional consequence.

Both address C7 (no gross developmental defects). OpenEval groups C7 with extensive background literature (C70-C90) as SUPPORTED citations. Peer review evaluates C7 separately, noting it's based on previous published work and accepted as premise for focusing on transcriptional changes.

Both address C70-C75 (background on SOCE, IP3/Ca2+ signaling, histone modifications). OpenEval groups with all background claims (C7, C70-C90) as literature citations. Peer review evaluates C70-C75 separately as established facts providing context, accepted without question.

Both address C76-C81 (background on Set2, Trl, CamKII). OpenEval groups with all background claims as literature citations. Peer review evaluates C76-C81 with C92 separately, accepting as part of mechanistic model linking SOCE to Trl activation including CamKII's role.

Both address C82-C90 (background on Trl properties and neuronal development). OpenEval groups with all background claims (C7, C70-C90) as literature citations. Peer review evaluates C82-C90 separately as established facts and bioinformatic analysis supporting Trl-mediated Set2 regulation.

Perfect alignment on C93 (integrative conclusion about Set2 regulating diverse gene classes). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes synthesis of multiple evidence lines. Peer review explicitly quotes this as 'noteworthy discovery' that 'SOCE regulates a wide range of neuronal genes...by controlling chromatin remodelling genes.'
